result.summary: Ensures that wallet replacement transactions generated by bumpfee do not have an nLockTime older than the transaction they replace. When creating a replacement, CCoinControl captures the original transaction's locktime as a minimum height floor for DiscourageFeeSniping. Random anti-fee-sniping backdating is then restricted between this minimum height and the current tip.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's anti-fee-sniping logic randomly backdates transaction locktimes by 0 to 99 blocks approximately 10% of the time for privacy. During RBF fee bumps, this random roll can result in a replacement transaction having a lower locktime than the original transaction, creating an unnatural on-chain pattern that leaks a fingerprint identifying the transaction as originating from Bitcoin Core or Electrum.
evidence: PR author mempool analysis of over 1,000,000 RBF transactions (2025-05 to 2026-06) found 200-300 backdated replacements per week (<2% of all replaced transactions): 'the few transactions that do exhibit backdating are easily fingerprintable as having been replaced using bumpfee in Bitcoin Core or Electrum.'
result.changed_since_previous: Added comprehensive unit and functional test coverage for the minimum height boundary conditions and stale tip handling in DiscourageFeeSniping.
result.card: This pull request ensures wallet fee-bumped transactions do not receive an nLockTime earlier than the transaction they replace. Anti-fee-sniping randomly backdates transaction locktimes by up to 99 blocks roughly 10% of the time, which can cause bumpfee to produce replacements with older locktimes than the original. This regression forms an on-chain fingerprint identifying Bitcoin Core or Electrum fee-bumped transactions. An empirical survey cited in the PR detected 200 to 300 backdated replacements per week, representing under 2% of surveyed RBF transactions.

risk.why: A flaw in locktime clamping could generate an invalid or unfinal transaction during bumpfee, preventing the fee bump from being broadcast.
